Observation, which this stage cannot repair: the engine's stale-review computation (iteration-0 probe, plus .scratch/run/work/install-publication-0001/w2-stale_paths.py) reports STALE-WEB-REVIEW, repair_target publication. Its sealed review_inputs differ only in source_publication/identities render sha256 and the three output digests derived from it. Content and evidence digests are unchanged. The render identity globs scripts/*.py (scripts/_document_schema.py, render_patterns), so the cause is scripts/_workflow.py, not this stage's release-record edits. publication-gates sets verify_review_inputs, so that gate will fail on this stale review before its checks run. Per the workflow, it routes to generate-web and a fresh web review. Separately, render identity covering every scripts/*.py means any engine-only edit invalidates accepted web reviews. That is worth a look by the tooling owner. Logs and timings are in .scratch/run/work/install-publication-0001/w2-*.
summary: Repaired the publication wiring after the driver's gate-runner commit (306cb81ea4, scripts/_workflow.py). That commit staled two things: the release binding for scripts/_workflow.py, and the browser-products families whose code closure includes it. The families were act-history, documents and web-editions. Only their generator component changed; content, rights, lock and membership did not. I re-recorded the browser products with `tools/browser-products record`, which exited 0 in 1260 s ('13 products, 27924 files; ok'). Only those three families' input commitments and keys changed, and their output bytes, counts and file sets stayed identical. I then ran two scoped refreshes without ADOPT, first `make refresh-release-bindings ONLY="scripts/_workflow.py"` and then `ONLY="release/browser-products.json"`, because the record rewrote that bound site source. Each refresh changed exactly one site_sources digest plus rights_record_sha256 and the rights-table digest row. Both forwarded gate commands now exit 0 under the engine's own `_run_gate_command` with its 1800 s budget. `make check-release-bindings` reported 'exact: 0 stale binding(s)' in 785.3 s. The document-catalogue command reported corpus.json current in 315.3 s.
